# Platform slices

<!-- Generated by scripts/generate-slices-doc.mjs from packages/platform-slices.json, packages/platform-slice-peers.json, packages/platform-slice-notes.json, the package.json exports and the slice READMEs. Do not edit: run `npm run docs:slices`. -->

> **Generated page.** Run `npm run docs:slices` after changing a slice, its README, its peers or its notes; `npm run check:slices-doc` (CI) fails when this page is stale. Hand-written facts live in [`packages/platform-slice-notes.json`](../packages/platform-slice-notes.json).

One page for every platform slice: what it is and gives you, which of the six packages carry it and the subpath imports, the admin cards and permissions it adds, the slices and peer dependencies it needs, and whether it can be used on its own. Design and rationale: [platform-packages spec](specs/platform-packages.md); documentation standard: [PACKAGES.md](PACKAGES.md).

## How slices, packages and npm relate

- **Six npm packages, one per layer**: `@marinoscar/platform-api` (NestJS), `@marinoscar/platform-web` (React and MUI), `@marinoscar/platform-contract` (zod wire shapes), `@marinoscar/platform-db` (schema fragments, migrations, seed), `@marinoscar/platform-cli` (the CLI factory, TUI, node engine) and `@marinoscar/platform-infra` (Compose, nginx and env fragments).
- **A slice is a subpath import, not a package.** `@marinoscar/platform-api/telemetry` and `@marinoscar/platform-web/telemetry/ui` are the telemetry slice in two packages. A capability usually spans several packages under one slice name; the "Carried by" column and each slice's table list them.
- **Slices form a graph** ([`packages/platform-slices.json`](../packages/platform-slices.json)): a slice may import only the slices listed for it. Depending on a slice costs no extra npm package, because it is in the same package; it costs that slice's peers and its wiring (host ports, settings, permissions).
- **Peers are per slice.** A package's `peerDependencies` are the union of what its slices need, but only what the always-needed slices (`core`) use is required; every other peer is `optional`. A slice's peers are its own plus those of its slice dependencies ([`packages/platform-slice-peers.json`](../packages/platform-slice-peers.json); rules in [PACKAGES.md](PACKAGES.md#peer-dependencies-per-slice)). npm does not install an optional peer, so an app installs the peers of the slices it imports.
- **Host ports keep slices apart.** A slice imports no app code; whatever it needs from the app (a database client, settings, an object store, the access decorators) is a port the app binds when it mounts the slice with `forRoot`.
- **Extending a slice.** Each slice README carries an Extension-point catalog of every registry, option, token binding, event and slot. [EXTENDING.md](EXTENDING.md) is the author guide (the ladder, the rule that an override goes through a `forRoot` binding, a recipe per extension, shipping an extension as its own npm package) and [EXTENSIBILITY-AUDIT.md](EXTENSIBILITY-AUDIT.md) records what each slice still closes.

The required peers of each package:

| Package | Required peers (needed by every slice of the package) |
|---|---|
| API (`@marinoscar/platform-api`) | `@nestjs/common`, `@nestjs/core`, `@nestjs/swagger`, `@opentelemetry/api`, `@prisma/client`, `nestjs-zod`, `reflect-metadata`, `rxjs`, `zod` |
| Web (`@marinoscar/platform-web`) | `@emotion/react`, `@emotion/styled`, `@mui/material`, `react`, `react-dom` |
| Contract (`@marinoscar/platform-contract`) | `zod` |
| DB (`@marinoscar/platform-db`) | `zod` |
| CLI (`@marinoscar/platform-cli`) | none |
| Infra (`@marinoscar/platform-infra`) | none |

## Slice index

Standalone: **Yes** means the slice imports and runs with the foundation slices only; **With slices** also needs the slices in "Needs", wired; **With app ports** also needs host ports or data the app supplies. Only the backend-only telemetry consumer is proven by a test ([below](#using-one-slice-on-its-own)); for every other slice the guarantee is the peer contract.

| [`core`](#core) | The registry primitive, the host ports, the principal and scope contract, the exception filter, the secret cipher and scoped data access every other API slice stands on; the host providers and API client adapter on the web; the command and env-spec registries in the CLI. | API, Web, CLI | none | Yes |
| [`testing`](#testing) | The conformance harness (`runPlatformConformance`, `runPlatformWebConformance`) that proves an app wires the slices correctly, and the shared test helpers. | API, Web, CLI | `core`, `engine` | Yes |

## Foundation slices

What every other slice stands on: the registry primitive and host ports, the OpenTelemetry core, the host plumbing, the permission manifest, the app shell and the data table.

### core

**What it gives you.** The registry primitive, the host ports, the principal and scope contract, the exception filter, the secret cipher and scoped data access every other API slice stands on; the host providers and API client adapter on the web; the command and env-spec registries in the CLI.

**What it is** (from its README). The bottom of the slice graph.

| Part | Import paths | Depends on (slices) | Install beyond the required peers | README |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| API (`platform-api`) | `/core`, `/core/testing` | none | none | [README](../packages/platform-api/src/core/README.md) |
| Web (`platform-web`) | `/core` | none | none | [README](../packages/platform-web/src/core/README.md) |
| CLI (`platform-cli`) | `/core` | none | none | [README](../packages/platform-cli/src/core/README.md) |

**Admin and settings cards.**

None.

**Permissions it adds.** none declared by this slice

**Standalone (Yes).** The bottom of every package graph, with no slice dependencies. In the API and web packages it is the only slice whose peers are required: an app that imports anything from the package installs them.

### testing

**What it gives you.** The conformance harness (`runPlatformConformance`, `runPlatformWebConformance`) that proves an app wires the slices correctly, and the shared test helpers.

**What it is** (from its README). The conformance harness.

| Part | Import paths | Depends on (slices) | Install beyond the required peers | README |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| API (`platform-api`) | `/testing` | `core` | none | [README](../packages/platform-api/src/testing/README.md) |
| Web (`platform-web`) | `/testing` | `core` | none | [README](../packages/platform-web/src/testing/README.md) |
| CLI (`platform-cli`) | `/testing` | `engine` | `react` | [README](../packages/platform-cli/src/testing/README.md) |

**Admin and settings cards.**

None.

**Permissions it adds.** none declared by this slice

**Standalone (Yes).** Import it from tests, never from application code. Each slice's own `/testing` entry point adds the suites that slice owns, and its peers. Transitive slice dependencies in API: `core`.

### doctor

**What it gives you.** The admin Doctor: a read-only check registry every slice adds its checks to, the report, the support bundle and the Doctor page.

**What it is** (from its README). The admin Doctor, `GET /api/admin/doctor`.

| Part | Import paths | Depends on (slices) | Install beyond the required peers | README |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| API (`platform-api`) | `/doctor` | `core` | `fastify` | [README](../packages/platform-api/src/doctor/README.md) |
| Web (`platform-web`) | `/doctor/headless`, `/doctor/ui` | `core` | `@mui/icons-material`, `react-router-dom` | [README](../packages/platform-web/src/doctor/README.md) |
| Contract (`platform-contract`) | `/doctor` | none | none | [README](../packages/platform-contract/src/doctor/README.md) |

**Admin and settings cards.**

| Card | Route | Permission | Feature gate | Declared by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Doctor | `/admin/settings/doctor` | `system_settings:read` | none | the package (data the app spreads into its registry) |

**Permissions it adds.** none declared by this slice

**Standalone (With slices).** The check registry and the report need only core. A check that probes another slice is registered by that slice, so it appears only when the app mounts it. Transitive slice dependencies in API: `core`.

### otel-core

**What it gives you.** The OpenTelemetry SDK behind a runtime export gate, the metric name registry and the `@Trace()` decorator, so a service emits traces and metrics without owning an exporter.

**What it is** (from its README). The **emitting** half of telemetry.

| Part | Import paths | Depends on (slices) | Install beyond the required peers | README |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| API (`platform-api`) | `/otel-core`, `/otel-core/sdk` | `core` | `fastify` | [README](../packages/platform-api/src/otel-core/README.md) |

**Admin and settings cards.**

None.

**Permissions it adds.** none declared by this slice

**Standalone (Yes).** Imports core only. Proven standalone by the backend-only consumer below: `OtelMetricsModule.forRoot()` boots and `@Trace()` runs. Transitive slice dependencies in API: `core`.

### telemetry

**What it gives you.** Observability for the app: the runtime-configured GreptimeDB connection, the SQL explorer, the AI assistant, the dashboard with its health verdict and metric groups, and the retention job.

**What it is** (from its README). The API side of observability, in the API layer: the `telemetry` settings and the runtime export gate they drive, the runtime GreptimeDB connection and client, the explorer (guarded SQL, schema, export), the AI assistant, the Telemetry Dashboard with its metric-group registry and health verdict, the stack-agent surface, and more.

| Part | Import paths | Depends on (slices) | Install beyond the required peers | README |

| API (`platform-api`) | `/telemetry`, `/telemetry/testing` | `core`, `doctor`, `otel-core` | `@nestjs/config`, `@nestjs/schedule`, `fastify`; `/testing` adds `@nestjs/platform-fastify` | [README](../packages/platform-api/src/telemetry/README.md) |
| Web (`platform-web`) | `/telemetry/headless`, `/telemetry/ui`, `/telemetry/ui/dashboard-page`, `/telemetry/ui/explorer-page`, `/telemetry/ui/settings-page` | `core` | `@codemirror/lang-sql`, `@mui/icons-material`, `@mui/x-charts`, `@mui/x-data-grid`, `@uiw/react-codemirror`, `react-router-dom` | [README](../packages/platform-web/src/telemetry/README.md) |
| Contract (`platform-contract`) | `/telemetry` | none | none | [README](../packages/platform-contract/src/telemetry/README.md) |
| CLI (`platform-cli`) | `/telemetry` | `core` | none | [README](../packages/platform-cli/src/telemetry/README.md) |
| Infra (`platform-infra`) | `/telemetry` | none | none | [README](../packages/platform-infra/src/telemetry/README.md) |

**Admin and settings cards.**

| Card | Route | Permission | Feature gate | Declared by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Telemetry | `/admin/settings/telemetry` | `telemetry:read` | none | the package (data the app spreads into its registry) |
| Telemetry Dashboard | `/admin/settings/telemetry/dashboard` | `telemetry:query` | `telemetry` | the package (data the app spreads into its registry) |
| Telemetry Explorer | `/admin/settings/telemetry/explorer` | `telemetry:query` | `telemetry` | the package (data the app spreads into its registry) |

**Permissions it adds.** `telemetry:{read,write,query}`

**Standalone (With app ports).** Imports core, otel-core and doctor. Mounting `TelemetryModule` additionally needs the app to bind the six telemetry host ports and to supply the access decorators; the backend-only consumer below imports it and builds its module metadata but does not boot it. Transitive slice dependencies in API: `core`, `doctor`, `otel-core`.

None.

Transitive slice dependencies in API: `ai`, `android-app`, `core`, `credentials`, `db-backup`, `doctor`, `email`, `exports`, `host`, `identity`, `jobs`, `nodes`, `notifications`, `otel-core`, `settings`, `sharing`, `storage`, `telemetry`, `user-data`.

## Feature slices

A capability an app mounts: its routes, jobs, settings, Doctor checks and, in the web package, its pages.

### sharing

**What it gives you.** Groups, members and invites inside an organization, group-owned resources, per-resource grants, link shares and the access policy that decides who can see a record.

**What it is** (from its README). The platform's sharing primitives: **groups** inside an organization, their **members** (roles `admin`, `editor`, `viewer`) and their **invites**, the **ownership contract** that lets an app table's row be owned by a user or by a group, and the **principal enrichment** that fills `Scope.groupIds`, and more.

| Part | Import paths | Depends on (slices) | Install beyond the required peers | README |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| API (`platform-api`) | `/sharing`, `/sharing/testing` | `core`, `doctor`, `otel-core` | `@nestjs/schedule`, `fastify` | [README](../packages/platform-api/src/sharing/README.md) |
| Web (`platform-web`) | `/sharing/headless`, `/sharing/ui` | `core` | `@mui/icons-material`, `react-router-dom` | [README](../packages/platform-web/src/sharing/README.md) |
| Contract (`platform-contract`) | `/sharing` | none | none | [README](../packages/platform-contract/src/sharing/README.md) |

**Admin and settings cards.**

| Card | Route | Permission | Feature gate | Declared by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Groups | `/settings/groups` | `groups:read` | none | the package (data the app spreads into its registry) |

**Permissions it adds.** `groups:{read,write,admin}` (org), `sharing:{read,write,admin}` (org)

**Standalone (With app ports).** Imports only core, doctor and otel-core; it does not import identity. The app declares which of its models are group-owned and binds the access policy through host ports. Transitive slice dependencies in API: `core`, `doctor`, `otel-core`.

## Tooling slices

The database, CLI and infrastructure tooling of the platform packages. They are subpath modules of the same packages, not features of the running app.

### compose

**What it gives you.** `platform db compose`: assembles the Prisma schema from the platform fragments and the app's own.

|---|---|---|---|---|
| DB (`platform-db`) | no subpath export | none | none | none |

**Admin and settings cards.**

None.

**Permissions it adds.** none declared by this slice

**Standalone (Yes).** Database tooling that imports no other slice. Run it from the app's `db:compose` script.

### lock

**What it gives you.** `platform.lock`: the checksums of every platform migration, and the check that an installed migration is never edited.

## Using one slice on its own

Slices are subpath imports of one npm package, so using one is a matter of importing only its subpaths and installing only its peers. Nothing else of the package loads, and the optional peers of every other slice stay out of `node_modules`.

The reference case is a backend-only telemetry consumer: `core`, `otel-core` and `telemetry` of `@marinoscar/platform-api`, nothing else. It is a real project, [`tests/consumer-smoke/api-slim`](../tests/consumer-smoke/api-slim/), that CI installs from packed tarballs outside the repository (see [the consumer smoke README](../tests/consumer-smoke/README.md)).

### Install

```bash
npm install @marinoscar/platform-api \
  @nestjs/common@^11.1.12 \
  @nestjs/config@^4.0.2 \
  @nestjs/core@^11.1.12 \
  @nestjs/schedule@^6.1.0 \
  @nestjs/swagger@^11.2.5 \
  @opentelemetry/api@^1.9.1 \
  @prisma/client@^7.8.0 \
  fastify@^5 \
  nestjs-zod@^5.4.0 \
  reflect-metadata@^0.2.2 \
  rxjs@^7.8.1 \
  zod@^4.4.3
```

That is `@nestjs/common`, `@nestjs/core`, `@nestjs/swagger`, `@opentelemetry/api`, `@prisma/client`, `nestjs-zod`, `reflect-metadata`, `rxjs`, `zod` (the package's required peers) plus `@nestjs/config`, `@nestjs/schedule`, `fastify` (the extra peers of `core`, `otel-core` and `telemetry`). The project's `dependencies` are validated against `packages/platform-slice-peers.json` by `npm run check:slices-doc`, so this list cannot drift from the slices it imports.

### The consumer

Copied from [`tests/consumer-smoke/api-slim/src/main.ts`](../tests/consumer-smoke/api-slim/src/main.ts):

```ts
import 'reflect-metadata';

import { applyDecorators, Injectable, Module } from '@nestjs/common';
import { NestFactory } from '@nestjs/core';
import { definePlatformHost } from '@marinoscar/platform-api/core';
import { MetricsHostService, OtelMetricsModule, Trace } from '@marinoscar/platform-api/otel-core';
import { TelemetryModule } from '@marinoscar/platform-api/telemetry';

@Injectable()
export class Greeter {
  @Trace()
  async hello(name: string): Promise<string> {
    return `hello ${name}`;
  }
}

@Module({ imports: [OtelMetricsModule.forRoot()], providers: [Greeter] })
export class SlimModule {}

/** A host whose access decorators do nothing: this consumer mounts no route. */
export const slimHost = definePlatformHost({
  access: {
    requirePermissions: () => applyDecorators(),
    requireAuthenticated: () => applyDecorators(),
  },
});

/** The module metadata `TelemetryModule.forRoot` builds (no boot: the telemetry ports are an app's to bind). */
export function telemetryModuleMetadata() {
  return TelemetryModule.forRoot({ host: slimHost, imports: [] });
}

export async function bootSlim() {
  const app = await NestFactory.createApplicationContext(SlimModule, { logger: false });
  return {
    app,
    greeter: app.get(Greeter),
    metrics: app.get(MetricsHostService),
  };
}
```

### What is proven, and what is not

The smoke test ([`tests/consumer-smoke/api-slim/test`](../tests/consumer-smoke/api-slim/test/)) proves:

- `@marinoscar/platform-api/core`, `@marinoscar/platform-api/otel-core`, `@marinoscar/platform-api/telemetry` load, and type-check under `NodeNext` with `skipLibCheck` off.
- `TelemetryModule.forRoot` returns its module metadata (module name, providers, controllers).
- A Nest application context boots on `OtelMetricsModule`, resolves `MetricsHostService` and runs a `@Trace()` method.
- The peers of the other slices (`@nestjs/jwt`, `@nestjs/passport`, `passport`, `@nestjs/event-emitter`, `@nestjs/terminus`, `@nestjs/platform-fastify`, `supertest`) are absent from `node_modules`.

It does **not** prove:

- **Booting `TelemetryModule`.** The module needs its 6 host ports bound by the app (`TELEMETRY_AUDIT_SINK`, `TELEMETRY_SETTINGS_STORE`, `TELEMETRY_CREDENTIAL_STORE`, `TELEMETRY_JOBS`, `TELEMETRY_AI`, `TELEMETRY_APP_INFO`) and the access decorators of the app's `definePlatformHost`. The smoke binds none of the ports and a dummy host.
- **Any other slice on its own.** For every slice, `npm run check:slice-peers` proves that the peers listed above cover its imports. That is the install contract; it is not a boot test.
- **The other packages.** The web, CLI, DB and infra packages are covered by the full consumers (`tests/consumer-smoke/api`, `tests/consumer-smoke/web`) and the starter, not by a slim one.

To use a different slice on its own, take its row in the tables above: import its paths, install its peers, bind the host ports its README lists, and mount it with its `forRoot`.

## Regenerating this page

```bash
npm run docs:slices         # write docs/SLICES.md
npm run check:slices-doc    # fail when it differs from the generated page or the notes are incomplete
```

A new slice needs, in the same change: its entry in `packages/platform-slices.json` and `packages/platform-slice-peers.json`, its README, and an entry in `packages/platform-slice-notes.json` (group, one-line "gives", standalone level and note, and the paths of any cards the app registers for it).
